Build a team's reference season from an MLB schedule

Source: R/season_games.R
season_games.Rd

Convert an MLB Stats API regular-season schedule into one row per completed game for one team, in the format compare_personal_season() expects.

Usage

season_games(schedule, team_id)

Arguments

schedule

Path or URL of a schedule JSON file, or the same response already parsed with jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = FALSE). Request it from https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/schedule?sportId=1&teamId=ID&season=YEAR&gameType=R.

team_id

MLB team identifier, such as 142 for the Minnesota Twins.

Value

A data frame sorted by date with character game_id, team, integer season, Date game_date, logical home, character opponent, integer runs, runs_allowed and run_diff, and 0/1 win.

Details

Only games played to completion are kept (coded status F), including games completed early. A postponed game appears in the schedule more than once under the same game_id, and its postponed entry also reports a final abstract state; it is kept once, when it was played. Ties and duplicated final games are errors. Reading a URL needs a network connection, so save the file first for reproducible work.

See also

compare_personal_season(), reviewed_team_seasons

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "schedule_sample.json", package = "daimondstats")
season_games(path, team_id = 142)
#>   game_id            team season  game_date  home            opponent runs
#> 1  746335 Minnesota Twins   2024 2024-03-28 FALSE  Kansas City Royals    4
#> 2  746804 Minnesota Twins   2024 2024-04-29 FALSE   Chicago White Sox    3
#> 3  745871 Minnesota Twins   2024 2024-08-09  TRUE Cleveland Guardians    6
#> 4  745927 Minnesota Twins   2024 2024-08-09  TRUE Cleveland Guardians    4
#>   runs_allowed run_diff win
#> 1            1        3   1
#> 2            2        1   1
#> 3            3        3   1
#> 4            2        2   1
